label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
**To the residents of Aughrim Terrace**

Someone has been putting full bags of rubbish into my grey Greenmount bin at No. 14, and I’ve had enough.

This isn’t the odd wrapper or a few bits put in by mistake. It’s been happening every week for about a month. Last Tuesday, I got home from work after a gig at 3am to find three black bags that weren’t mine stuffed into it, including one containing nappies. The lid wouldn’t even close.

My bin is charged by weight, at €0.41 a kilo. My last bill was €63.20 for two months, when it’s usually around €25. I’m paying to get rid of my own rubbish, not to quietly cover somebody else’s as well.

The bin has **14 painted in white on the lid**, so there should be no confusion about whose it is. It goes out on Tuesday night for collection on Wednesday morning. Being out on the road for collection does not make it a free bin for the terrace.

I work nights. That means I’m often not home in the evening, not that I won’t notice three extra bags of rubbish or a bill more than twice what I normally pay. I’ve noticed, and I’m not prepared to keep footing it.

If you’re stuck with rubbish and don’t know what to do with it, ask. I’ll tell you who to ring. There are ways of sorting it that don’t involve leaving a neighbour to pay for it without their permission.

I don’t know who’s doing this, which is why this letter is going to everyone. Apologies to the neighbours who have nothing to do with it.

To whoever is responsible: **stop putting your rubbish in my bin.** If it continues, I’ll be putting a padlock on it.

I’d much rather not have to lock my own bin to get that basic bit of consideration.

**No. 14**
